title: Data terms
description: The disclosure regime for THIS process's own records — the co-produced private data behind the agreement's merkle leaves (the agreement content, the evidence, the books each side keeps). Absent this clause the paper-contract default applies: each party holds its own copy and may disclose it. Composing this clause makes the regime an explicit, co-signed agreement term: the designer sets the regime at design time (the design-canvas card's disclosure toggle writes the disclosure field into the template), and the buyer commits a per-order choice over their own half at checkout — the same fill pattern as the modality clause. Sealed per-order encrypted fields (delivery addresses, counterparty-private hand-off content) sit outside every regime by construction and are never disclosable through this clause. What a party then DOES with its disclosable records — what is offered for sale, to whom, when, at what price — is a catalogue and profile concern, never fields here; the terms of a specific data sale are the data-license clause's concern. This clause is composed by designers and selected by buyers; it is never article-mandatory — a disclosure regime is a choice, and regime variants are sibling assemblies.

fields.name: disclosure

valueLabels.each-own: Each party may disclose its own copy

fields.description: The regime for the process's co-produced records, fixed by the designer at design time. closed = neither party discloses beyond the parties (the composed confidentiality term); each-own = each party may disclose the copy it holds (the paper-contract default, made explicit and co-signed); open = either party may publish the process record.

fields.name: buyerDisclosure
fields.description: The buyer's per-order choice over their own half of the record, filled at checkout and committed at signing. withhold = content the buyer contributed must be excluded or redacted from any disclosure the regime otherwise allows; permit = it may travel with the disclosed record. Moot under a closed regime, but always committed — consent is explicit, never inferred.
